# Helping your midwife find you
## A warm welcome from Riverside Community Midwives

When you call us to say your baby may be on the way, we want to spend our time looking after you — not looking for your front door.

Sat nav is helpful, but it does not know everything. It can lead us to the wrong building, the back of your house or, occasionally, somewhere selling chips. Lovely on another day. Not quite what we need when a baby is coming.

A few small things can help us reach you quickly, with our bags, equipment and energy still in one piece.

Think of this as helping a friend find your home for the first time. A friend carrying rather more than a handbag.

## First things first: when to call

**Riverside home birth cover starts at 37 weeks of pregnancy.**

If you think labour is starting **before 37 weeks**, contact the hospital maternity team straight away. You will need hospital care rather than the home birth service. Do not wait for your next appointment.

**From 37 weeks, phone the Riverside birth line when you think labour is starting.** You do not need to be certain before you call. The midwife can talk with you about what is happening and what to do next.

Please use the **birth line, not your usual midwife’s personal mobile**. The birth line reaches the midwife on call. Your usual midwife may be off duty, asleep or looking after another family.

**Call rather than sending a WhatsApp message to ask for care.** Messages and location pins are helpful for directions, but they do not replace a phone call.

When you call, tell us:

- Your name and how many weeks pregnant you are.
- What is happening, including whether your waters have broken.
- Your full address and postcode.
- A phone number we can call you back on.
- Any important details about finding or entering your home.

If you have concerns such as bleeding or your baby moving less than usual, contact maternity care straight away rather than waiting for labour. In a life-threatening emergency, call **999**. If you think the baby is coming right now and no midwife is with you, call **999** and follow the call handler’s instructions.

## Help us find the right front door

Please check that we have your full address, including your house or flat number, building name and postcode. Let us know if you move during pregnancy.

If your house has a name instead of a number, tell us exactly what the sign says. “Rosemary Cottage” may sound easy to spot, but it is less helpful if the sign is hidden behind a hedge.

Useful directions might be:

- “Our entrance is on the side road, not the main road.”
- “We are the house with the blue door, opposite the pharmacy.”
- “The sat nav takes you to the back. Please use the front entrance on Mill Lane.”
- “Flat 14 is in the second building, not the building with flat 13.”

That last one matters more than you might think. Flat numbers do not always follow the rules the rest of us expect.

If you live in a block of flats, please tell us:

- Which building and entrance to use.
- Your floor and flat number.
- Which buzzer to press.
- Any entry code we will need.
- Whether there is a lift, and whether it is working.

If the buzzer is broken or the entrance is hard to find, let us know before labour if possible. We would much rather make a plan together than have someone waving a tea towel from an upstairs window at 3am.

## A pin can help — but please phone first

If your home is difficult to find, you can send a **location pin on WhatsApp to the Riverside birth line phone**. A **what3words location** can also help identify the entrance.

Please check that the pin or three-word address points to the door we should use, rather than the middle of the building, a back garden or a nearby road.

Give us your full address as well. A location pin is an extra clue, not a replacement.

For your privacy, send directions and entry codes directly to the team. **Please do not put your address, access code or location pin in the Facebook group.**

## Light the way

At night, please turn on your porch or outside light if you have one. A hallway light can help too.

Check that your house number or name is easy to see from the street. You know which door is yours. In the dark, we may be looking at a whole row of very similar doors.

An easy-to-spot marker can help. One family used balloons on the gate — a lovely welcome and excellent directions. If you use a balloon, ribbon or sign, secure it safely, keep the path clear and tell us what to look for.

There is no need to decorate the whole street. We are coming for a birth, not judging a garden party.

## Two midwives, usually two cars

**Two midwives attend the birth, usually travelling in separate cars.** If possible, please arrange two parking spaces close to your home.

We carry quite a lot: gas and air cylinders, a large birth bag and sometimes equipment for a birthing pool. The shorter and clearer the route, the sooner we can get everything inside.

If you cannot provide parking, please do not worry. Tell us where we can safely and legally park, and whether there is a walk from the car.

Some streets around **Anfield and Kensington** have parking restrictions or permit requirements. Check the rules for your street with the council before your due date. If visitor permits are needed, ask how to arrange them and have them ready for both cars.

Some permits need to be displayed in the vehicle; others need to be activated digitally. Let us know what applies. Please do not assume that a midwife’s car is exempt from parking restrictions.

## A clear path, not a perfect house

Please clear the route from your front door to the room where we will be caring for you. If we need to use the stairs, keep those clear too.

Shoes, bags, washing baskets and trailing cables can be difficult to see when we are carrying equipment. Lego is especially good at finding a foot at the worst possible moment.

**You do not need to clean the whole house.** We are not checking your skirting boards. A safe, clear route and space for our equipment are what matter.

If there are steps, a narrow passage or another access difficulty, tell us beforehand so we can plan with you.

## Pets: much loved, safely out of the way

Please settle pets in another room or secure area before we arrive, away from our route into the house.

We know your dog may be friendly. They may be *very* friendly. But an excited welcome can make it difficult to carry a gas and air cylinder safely.

Give pets somewhere comfortable, with water and whatever they need. If you have an assistance dog, talk with us beforehand so we can make a suitable plan together.

## Letting us in

If someone is with you, they can listen for the door or meet us at the entrance. **Nobody needs to leave you alone to look for us.**

You do not need to leave your front door unlocked. Agree a safe way for us to get in, keep your phone nearby and tell us if knocking or ringing the bell will not work.

An open door alone does not tell us we have found the right house. We would rather check than surprise your neighbour — even if they do offer a biscuit.

## Your fridge checklist

### Helping our midwives find us

**Riverside birth line:** ______________________________

**Hospital maternity contact:** _______________________

**Our full address and postcode:**  
__________________________________________________

**Useful entrance or parking directions:**  
__________________________________________________

### Before 37 weeks
☐ Save the birth line and hospital maternity numbers.  
☐ Check the team has our correct address and phone number.  
☐ Explain any tricky entrances, stairs, gates or broken buzzers.  
☐ Check parking rules and arrange visitor permits if needed.  
☐ Remember: labour before 37 weeks needs hospital care.

### When labour starts
☐ **Phone the Riverside birth line — not a personal mobile.**  
☐ Give our address and explain how to find the entrance.  
☐ Send a location pin if helpful, after calling.  
☐ Arrange two parking spaces if possible; have permits ready.  
☐ Turn on the outside light at night.  
☐ Clear the hallway, stairs and route to the birth room.  
☐ Settle pets safely away from the entrance and equipment.  
☐ Keep the phone nearby and agree how to let the midwives in.

**No perfect house needed. Just help us find you, and we will take it from there. We look forward to caring for you and welcoming your baby.**

*Riverside Community Midwives*
